text: Security is a vital part of web development. First, websites should use HTTPS to encrypt data between the user and the server. Second, authentication helps confirm that users are who they claim to be, usually through strong passwords or two-factor methods. Third, input validation checks all data coming from users, which helps prevent attacks such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting. Developers must also learn about common vulnerabilities, like broken access control and insecure storage, so they can fix them early. By following these basic rules, developers can build safer websites and protect users' personal information.
